title: Camp 2 close: the cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1)
hookLine: the saints aren't statues but a crowd cheering you on
carry: so great a cloud of witnesses
tomorrow: First Mass, or first in years

lines: BOTH SIDES OF THE STREET, PACKED.
cards: The last mile of a marathon. The legs are gone and the lungs are burning. Then the runner turns a corner, and both sides of the street are packed.
Strangers, shouting the name on the bib. Some ran this race last year; some ran it decades ago. They know this mile, and they're yelling: keep going, nearly there.
An early Christian writer used a picture much like it in the Letter to the Hebrews. It's the picture Catholics have in mind when they look at a church full of saints. Not statues.

teach.h: A ROLL CALL IN HEBREWS ELEVEN.
teach.b: Hebrews chapter eleven is a roll call of people who kept faith: Abel, Noah, Abraham and Sarah, Moses, Rahab, and many more the writer runs out of time to name. Then chapter twelve turns to the reader.
In the Douay-Rheims: "having so great a cloud of witnesses over our head," let us lay down every weight and run the race. A cloud, not a handful.
The Greek word for witness is martys, which later gave us martyr: witnesses who have finished, watching the ones still running.
In the Apostles' Creed, said at baptisms and at the start of the rosary, Catholics say they believe in the communion of saints: the Church as one family across death.
Catholics speak of it in three parts: those still on earth, those being made ready for God, and those already with God in heaven. Love goes across all three.

That's why Catholics pray for the dead, and ask the saints to pray for them, the way you'd ask a friend. Think back over this camp. Two pregnant women meeting in the hill country, and a child with no room at the inn.
Fishermen, a woman at a well, a man through a roof, a lost son, a Samaritan on the road. A garden, a cross, an empty tomb, a road to Emmaus. Fire at Pentecost.
Mary. Then the saints: Augustine, Patrick, Clare, Catherine, Joan, More, Bernadette, Thérèse, Kolbe, Teresa.

teach.h: SO GREAT A CLOUD OF WITNESSES.
teach.b: Catholics would say that's not a list of the dead. That's the crowd on the street.

how: Catholics profess the communion of saints in the Apostles' Creed, pray for the dead especially in November and on All Souls' Day, keep All Saints' Day on November 1, and often choose a patron saint at baptism or confirmation.

o: a monastery where the saints once lived together
the Church as one family across death
a gathering of all the bishops in Rome

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: a roll call of people who kept faith

s: the word martyr comes from a Greek word for witness
martys: a witness. the cloud in Hebrews is a cloud of witnesses.
the communion of saints means only the well-known saints in heaven
Catholics mean the whole Church across death: on earth, being made ready, and in heaven.
Catholics ask the saints to pray for them the way you'd ask a friend
love goes across death, so they pray for the dead and ask the saints' prayers.

games.q: you're the writer of Hebrews. you've just listed Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses and more. how do you turn to your readers?
o: tell them to build statues to these heroes.
tell them these heroes are watching, so run the race.
tell them no one today can match these heroes.
games.why: the writer pictures a cloud of witnesses over our head, and says: lay down every weight and run the race.

practice: Let one face from this camp's stories come forward: the one who surprised you, maybe, or the one most like you, or least.
Don't choose the most impressive; choose the one you'd want beside you on a bad day, a saint to walk with this year, and say their name once, quietly. If you pray, you can ask them to pray for you.

wordCard.voice: communio sanctorum. Latin for the communion of saints, the Church as one family across death, in prayer for each other.

orig.note: Latin: the communion of saints, the phrase in the Apostles' Creed.

carryVoice: Your line: so great a cloud of witnesses. Tomorrow Camp Three, the practices, starts at the church door. That's Camp Two, done.
